lacuna.repo_anchor: plan/0010-last-fifth/README.md #corpus lists "small-batch parallelism" in the approved nine-item corpus and #surgeries names "small-batch-parallelism restructuring" among the schedulable surgery classes. research/decode-step-scheduling/outline.yaml defines the item: "SOTA parallelization of decode attention at batch 4-8 - split axis vs head-batching vs persistent scheduling at 0.17-wave occupancy". The occupancy premise is host-measured: at the short shape the bridge walk kernel launches grid (num_reqs, h_kv, splits) = (4-8, 4, 1-2) = 8-32 CTAs (turing_lab/bridge/bridge_paged_decode_split.cu:247,254: dim3 grid(num_reqs, h_kv, splits)), which is 0.06-0.22 waves against 72 SMs x 2-4 resident CTAs [derived; the brief's "84 SMs (TU102)" figure matches GA102, not stock TU102/Quadro RTX 6000 = 72 SMs - uncertain, use the queried SM count at init]. PROFILE-DELTA.md records the complementary long-ctx fact: post-surgery walk DRAM 51-58 pct while waves are full at ctx2048 (8x4x64=2048 CTAs at PPS2) - so sub-wave occupancy is the SHORT-shape disease and per-CTA memory-level parallelism is the long-ctx one. MEMORY.md 2026-09-13: champion 41.3/41.2/195.5 = 0.82 of the TRITON 50.1 baseline, floor 0.75, and the sensitivity-floor lesson: "only multi-ms per-step kernel deltas move the committed rows".
lacuna.current_status: As of 2026-09-15 the decode-attention parallelization literature is mature and converges on one observation: at decode, natural parallelism is batch x heads (here 4-8 x 4 KV heads = 16-32 CTAs), which sub-fills any datacenter or pro GPU, and the fix is to add work axes. (1) FlashDecoding (PyTorch blog + Stanford CRFM, 2023-10-12) adds the KV-sequence axis: split KV into chunks, run partial online-softmax per chunk in parallel, reduce with per-split log-sum-exp. Its split-count heuristic is published in source - Dao-AILab/flash-attention flash_api.cpp:263-297 (read 2026-09-15 at tag v2.7.4.post1, commit 5231d95f): if batch_nheads_mblocks >= 0.8f * num_SMs return 1 split; else max_splits = min(max_splits, num_SMs, num_n_blocks); score each eligible split count by wave efficiency eff = n_waves/ceil(n_waves) with n_waves = batch_nheads_mblocks * num_splits / num_SMs, and return the SMALLEST split count with eff >= 0.85 * max_efficiency; a split count is eligible only if it actually changes blocks-per-split (avoids padding splits). Issue #609 (2023-10-17) confirms num_splits=0 triggers this heuristic and it depends on GPU/batch/heads. Note the FA2 decode grid already merges (batch, head) into one grid axis - the merged-axis structure is standard, not novel. (2) FlashInfer (arXiv 2501.01005, 2025-01; scheduler read via DeepWiki 2026-09-15): plan/run API precomputes split metadata once per shape and reuses it across layers; the decode scheduler uses PartitionPagedKVCacheBinarySearchMinNumPagePerBatch (scheduler.cuh:73-99) - a binary search for the minimum pages-per-batch that satisfies grid-size constraints - plus work-estimation dispatch on GROUP_SIZE/HEAD_DIM; non-persistent partitioned kernels reduce via MergeStateKernel, or a PERSISTENT variant BatchPagedAttentionPersistent keeps a fixed resident CTA count fetching work from a global queue to cut launch overhead and tail latency. FlashInfer's README GPU support table lists Turing SM 7.5 (T4, RTX 20xx) as supported (issue #2579 repeats SM75 in the supported list); the engine-side caveat: vLLM v0.24.0 (2026-06-29) dropped FlashInfer from sm75 backend candidates, v0.23.0 last-good (host lacuna record). (3) TensorRT-LLM multiblock attention (NVIDIA dev blog, 2024-11-21): splits decode KV across SMs and aggregates partials back; motivation sentence matches this item exactly ("typically runs on only a few SMs, leaving the rest idle", worst at small batch, long sequences, and per-GPU under model parallelism); measured up to 3.5x tokens/s at long-sequence low-batch on H200; runtime heuristic decides single- vs multi-block, with real-world misjudgment cases (issue #1548, multi-block perf regression); the FA4-era changelog adds "split-KV heuristic for low-occupancy cross-attention". (4) LeanAttention (arXiv 2405.10480, 2024-05, MLSys 2025): treats the online softmax as a reduction and extends stream-K tiling to decode attention - a persistent, load-balanced tile walk over flattened (batch, head, KV-chunk) LeanTiles; avg 2.6x over FA2 on decode, up to 8.33x at 512k context [paper abstract figures; batch-4-8 short-ctx cells not extracted - uncertain]. (5) FlashDecoding++ (arXiv 2311.01282, 2023-11, MLSys 2024): replaces the per-split running max with a unified max so partials need no cross-CTA synchronization; 1.37x avg over serving engines incl. FlashDecoding, benchmarked on A100 and RTX 3090 - numerics-approximate, see failure_modes. (6) Cooperative launch: cooperative_groups grid.sync() requires a fully co-resident grid (cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor) and IS permitted inside CUDA graphs - CUDA Programming Guide (graphs chapter, accessed 2026-09-15): "Cooperative launches are permitted so long as MPS is not in use"; production attention stacks mostly avoid grid sync in favor of second-kernel or atomic-ticket reduction anyway (NVIDIA forum threads 320600/341549). (7) Persistent/megakernel line (single persistent kernel for whole decode, kog.ai MI300X 2025; ForgeMegakernel alphaXiv 2609.12379 [uncertain: date]; CUTLASS persistent/stream-K tutorial, Colfax 2024) - belongs to the sibling corpus item megakernels-persistent-decode; here it matters only as the ceiling of the persistent-scheduler direction. (8) Head-axis economics: FA2/FA3 PackGQA packs the GQA q-heads INTO the M tile so one CTA serves a KV head's whole group, and is forced ON for paged/split kernels (flash-attention instantiated that way per repo docs read 2026-09-15) - packing is the right choice when work is plentiful; at SUB-WAVE shapes the published logic inverts: the GQA axis is the one axis with spare parallelism, and unpacking it (one CTA per (req, q_head)) multiplies the grid by g with NO cross-CTA reduction, because q-head outputs are independent; the cost is g-fold K/V re-reads, which at this host is bounded by the 0.12 ms/step KV-traffic wall. (9) Local control: the winning TRITON baseline at the host pin is ITSELF a two-stage fixed-split design - vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_decode_attention.py:232 grid = (batch, head_num, NUM_KV_SPLITS) with kv_len_per_split = tl.cdiv(cur_batch_seq_len, NUM_KV_SPLITS) (line 117: per-request adaptive lengths, shape-static count, graph-friendly) and a fixed stage-2 reduce. The 50.1 tok/s baseline does NOT win by avoiding splits; it wins with the same split-KV structure the bridge has, so the bridge's deficit is in sizing/placement, not in the pattern.
lacuna.applicability: The bridge already IS a FlashDecoding-class split-KV kernel (walk + combine), so the SOTA delta reduces to three adoptable restructurings, all sm_75-clean (none needs cp.async/TMA/clusters; Turing mma is irrelevant here since the walk is a 256-thread FMA kernel with 1 KB staging smem post-surgery). (A) SPLIT SIZING: replace the fixed PAGES_PER_SPLIT derivation (splits = cdiv(max_pages, PPS), sized for the WORST request per the .cu comment) with the FA2 wave-efficiency rule evaluated at capture time per (batch, max_pages) - static under graphs, matching how the TRITON baseline keeps NUM_KV_SPLITS constexpr-static. At batch 4-8 x 4 KV heads, 16-32 CTAs never reach the 0.8-fill early-out on 72 SMs, so the rule always splits; what it buys is principled PPS selection per shape instead of the hand-swept knee at 1-2 (host record). (B) HEAD-AXIS UNPACK: regrid the walk from (req, h_kv, splits) to (req, h_q, splits) or flattened req*h_q - at 24Q/4KV this is a 6x grid multiplier exactly where splits cannot help (short ctx has no KV to split further); zero extra reduction, g-fold K/V re-reads bounded by ~0.12 ms at the wall; needs the float workspace re-indexed per q-head (see failure_modes - this is where it likely dies). (C) FUSED REDUCTION: fold combine into the walk via last-CTA-wins atomic ticket per (req, kv_head) - removes one launch and the workspace round-trip for all 8 full-attn layers every step, the same structure FlashInfer ships as threadblock_sync_state/MergeState and TRT-LLM as multiblock aggregation. (D) PERSISTENT walk (FlashInfer BatchPagedAttentionPersistent / LeanAttention style): grid = resident capacity, dynamic (req, head, chunk) tile fetch - the SOTA ceiling, also balances variable per-request seq lens; co-residency under cooperative launch is NOT required if tiles fetch via a device-global counter instead. Cooperative grid.sync is legal here (graphs allowed, no MPS on this host) but caps the grid at resident capacity - the atomic-ticket form is more portable. What does NOT transfer: FA3/FA4 TMA/cluster multicast and warp-specialization machinery (sm_80+); FlashDecoding++'s unified-max softmax (numerics, below); TRT-LLM/XQA tensor-core decode paths. Transfer risk unique to this host: the short-row ENGINE-CONTEXT INVERSION (MEMORY.md 2026-09-13: walk kernel 3x FASTER isolated at the short shape yet the step 3.6 ms slower, mechanism OPEN) means an isolated-occupancy win can land engine-negative - committed A/B is the only verdict.

design.mechanism: Two-stage plan against the split walk/combine kernels as they exist at the pin (register-accumulator champion, NTHREADS=256, 1 KB smem staging, PPS build-time -DPAGES_PER_SPLIT). STAGE 1 - principled split sizing (engine-lane, no kernel change): at graph capture, per (batch_size, max_pages), compute the split count with the FA2 rule transplanted verbatim: CTA_base = num_reqs * h_kv; if CTA_base >= 0.8 * num_SMs use 1 split; else for s = 1..min(num_SMs, n_blocks) pick the smallest eligible s with wave efficiency >= 0.85 * max (eligibility: cdiv(n_blocks, s) != cdiv(n_blocks, s-1)); set PPS = cdiv(max_pages, s) for that capture. num_SMs from torch.cuda.get_device_properties(...).multi_processor_count (72 expected on TU102 [uncertain vs brief's 84]); n_blocks = cdiv(max_pages, block_size). This subsumes the PPS sweep's knee-at-1-2 finding into a shape-static rule and is oracle-inert (same kernel, different grid.z). STAGE 2 - fused single-launch reduction (kernel-lane): add to the walk kernel an epilogue - each walk CTA atomically increments a per-(req, kv_head) arrival counter (an int in the workspace, zeroed before replay - the cuda-graph-atomic-reduction lacuna's zeroing requirement) after writing its partials; the LAST arriving CTA (ticket == splits-1) immediately runs the existing combine math for its (req, kv_head) reading all splits' partials in FIXED split-index order (never completion order - determinism). Grid and launch config otherwise unchanged; one kernel replaces two per layer per step (8 launches/step removed); num arrivals per (req, head) is shape-static in splits. The walk's early-exit CTAs (pos >= seq_len break at the .cu's page loop) still count as arrived - they must participate in the ticket even when they did no work, which is exactly the host's DIVERGENT-BARRIER lesson generalized: every CTA in the grid executes the epilogue unconditionally. DEFERRED candidates, priced but not first: (B) head-axis unpack - regrid y from h_kv to h_q, workspace ws_m/ws_l/ws_o re-indexed {reqs, h_q, splits, ...} (6x float workspace at equal splits) or per-(kv_head, split) atomic merge (breaks the fp32 fixed-order class); gate-1 cull it by arithmetic before writing code: it only pays if the ledger prices short-shape walk+combine >= ~1 ms/step. (D) persistent walk - grid = min(tiles, resident capacity) with a device-global tile counter; adopt only if the chrome-trace shows tail/launch gaps the fused reduction does not already close.
design.failure_modes: (1) Over-split economics is the measured host failure: the PPS knee at 1-2 (constraint frame; PPS1 halves workspace and combine reads) is exactly the FA2 rule's warning side - splits beyond fill add partials traffic and combine reads for zero latency. The transplanted rule inherits FA2's eligibility check and caps (num_SMs, num_n_blocks) precisely to avoid this; still expect the rule to AGREE with the hand sweep at most shapes, making stage 1 a hygiene win, not a tok/s win. (2) Workspace growth: the head-unpack variant multiplies float workspace 6x - rhymes with the PPS-knee mechanism (partials volume is the cost) and with half2 staging NO_DIFF (MEMORY.md 2026-09-13: a strictly-better isolated kernel landed NO_DIFF engine-side when it cut ~0.1-0.5 ms/step) - predicted non-mover; cull on arithmetic. (3) Determinism: atomic-ticket ordering must not leak into the numerics - the finisher merges partials in fixed split-index order; atomicAdd of fp32 partials (FlashDecoding-style) is REJECTED (breaks the oracle's 6e-5-class bit discipline and re-opens the Thinking-Machines nondeterminism class the host's cuda-graph-atomic-reduction lacuna records: workspace zeroing between replays is already a standing requirement). (4) Cross-CTA sync bugs: last-CTA-wins reintroduces the DIVERGENT-BARRIER class the host already caught once (plan/0009 C2: per-warp any_alive let idle warps skip a barrier - dims 0-63 correct, 64+ corrupt, single-token exact); defense named: unconditional epilogue participation, oracle >= 18/18 across dims and seq_len classes including the seq_len < q_len degenerate row, plus the per-arm-logprob third-reference test. (5) KV-pipelining rhyme: any staging/prefetch dressed up as part of this restructure inherits the falsified lever - KV read pipelining measured NEGATIVE (ctx512 -11.5 pct, MEMORY.md 2026-09-13); keep the memory path byte-identical. (6) Graph replay: split count and arrival counters must be static per capture (they are: function of batch and max_pages); counter zeroing must ride the existing per-replay workspace clear, not a host-side memset per step. (7) Cooperative-launch variant: legal in graphs (CUDA guide, no MPS here) but caps grid at resident capacity - conflicts with (A)'s fill goal and adds cudaLaunchCooperativeKernel API friction in the torch extension; atomic-ticket is the portable form. (8) Engine-context inversion: even a correct, isolated-faster kernel can regress the committed short row (3x-faster/3.6ms-slower record is unexplained) - gate-0 plus the committed medians-of-3 protocol is mandatory before any champion-row claim.
design.effort_estimate: Stage 1 (sizing rule): engine-lane, one session - a capture-time integer computation plus a gate-0 rerun; cull cost trivial. Stage 2 (fused reduction): kernel-lane 1-2 sessions - walk epilogue + ticket + fixed-order merge, oracle sweep, graph replay check, one gate-1 ladder row, committed A/B. Deferred (B)/(D): 1-2 and 2-4 sessions respectively, only if the step-profile ledger prices them above the floor. Total recommended spend before evidence: 2-3 sessions.
design.priority_signal: AGAINST as a standalone multi-ms lever, and the arithmetic should be stated plainly: the 0.17-wave shape is the SHORT row, where the walk kernel is 80.6 us isolated x 8 layers = ~0.65 ms/step [derived from the MEMORY.md 2026-09-13 isolation record] - perfect utilization cannot recover more than a fraction of that, far under the sensitivity floor (only multi-ms per-step deltas move committed rows). At ctx2048 - the row where the 4.3 ms gap to TRITON lives - the walk is already multi-wave (2048 CTAs at PPS2), so occupancy restructuring does not touch the measured gap there; PROFILE-DELTA pins the long-ctx limiter at DRAM 51-58 pct with full waves, which is per-CTA memory-level parallelism, and its lever (KV pipelining) is FALSIFIED NEGATIVE on this host. FOR, on two honest hooks: (i) the fused reduction (stage 2) is not an occupancy trick but a launch-count/round-trip removal that runs at BOTH shapes - 8 launches/step removed multiplies with the graph-node-concurrency item, and the OPEN 3.6 ms short-row inversion (kernel faster isolated, step slower engine-side) is exactly the class of engine-level structure this surgery could dodge or expose - the chrome-trace diff named as its follow-up instrument is the same instrument that prices this item; (ii) stages 1-2 are cheap and oracle-first, so the cull cost is small. Net: schedule stage 1 + stage 2 behind #step-profile as a paired surgery; retire the head-unpack (B) unless the ledger prices short-shape attention >= 1 ms/step; treat persistent (D) as the megakernels item's tenant. If the ledger attributes the short-row inversion to NCCL/graph scheduling instead of launch structure, record the row and retire the whole item as bounded below the floor.
